#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A/B speed and memory of this checkout (or a branch) against origin/main, for when a change touches the resolver.

Builds both in release mode, then times `extract --json` over Mantine and Chakra (source directory only, no
dependencies, fetched once into .corpora/) with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first, and prints
the median wall time and peak RSS of each side. Calibrated on CI runners and a laptop: with nothing changed, the ratio
stays within 1.04 for time and 1.12 for memory, so more than 1.10x in time or 1.20x in memory is worth a look. Nothing
enforces that.

Usage: scripts/bench.py [BRANCH] [--runs N] [--corpus NAME]...   (BRANCH defaults to this checkout, uncommitted work included)
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import tempfile

import corpora
from corpora import ROOT, run_once


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def build(manifest_dir, target_dir, destination):
    subprocess.run(['cargo', 'build', '--release', '--locked', '-p', 'caliper-docgen', '--manifest-path',
                    os.path.join(manifest_dir, 'Cargo.toml'), '--target-dir', target_dir], check=True)
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(target_dir, 'release', 'caliper-docgen'), destination)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('branch', nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('--runs', type=int, default=9)
    parser.add_argument('--corpus', action='append')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.corpus = args.corpus or ['mantine', 'chakra']
    subprocess.run(['git', 'fetch', '-q', 'origin', 'main'], cwd=ROOT)
    target = os.path.join(ROOT, 'target')
    trees = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        try:
            base_tree = os.path.join(tmp, 'base')
            git('worktree', 'add', '--detach', base_tree, git('rev-parse', '--verify', 'origin/main^{commit}'))
            trees.append(base_tree)
            build(base_tree, target, os.path.join(tmp, 'base-bin'))
            head_tree = ROOT
            if args.branch:
                head_tree = os.path.join(tmp, 'head')
                git('worktree', 'add', '--detach', head_tree, git('rev-parse', '--verify', f'{args.branch}^{{commit}}'))
                trees.append(head_tree)
            build(head_tree, target, os.path.join(tmp, 'head-bin'))
            builds = {'base': os.path.join(tmp, 'base-bin'), 'head': os.path.join(tmp, 'head-bin')}
            corpora_dir = os.path.abspath(corpora.DEFAULT_DIR)
            print(f"{'corpus':<9} {'base ms':>8} {'head ms':>8} {'ratio':>6}   {'base MiB':>8} {'head MiB':>8} {'ratio':>6}")
            for corpus in corpora.selected(args.corpus):
                src = corpora.source_dir(corpus, corpora_dir)
                command = lambda binary: [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--no-cache', '--no-load-dependencies']
                samples = {'base': [], 'head': []}
                for label, binary in builds.items():
                    run_once(command(binary))
                for i in range(args.runs):
                    for label in (('base', 'head') if i % 2 == 0 else ('head', 'base')):
                        samples[label].append(run_once(command(builds[label])))
                median = {label: (statistics.median(s for s, _ in runs) * 1000, statistics.median(r for _, r in runs))
                          for label, runs in samples.items()}
                (bt, br), (ht, hr) = median['base'], median['head']
                print(f"{corpus['name']:<9} {bt:8.0f} {ht:8.0f} {ht / bt:6.2f}   {br:8.0f} {hr:8.0f} {hr / br:6.2f}")
        finally:
            for tree in trees:
                subprocess.run(['git', 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', tree], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The five public repos Caliper is measured on, fetched at pinned commits. Shared by weekly.py and bench.py.

`setup` fetches each repo, installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off,
caches under the corpora directory's parent), and prunes tests, stories and demos from the source directory. With
--sparse it fetches only the source directory and installs nothing: enough for `just bench`, which turns dependency
loading off.

Usage: scripts/corpora.py setup [--corpora DIR] [--corpus NAME]... [--sparse] [--install-node-dir DIR]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DEFAULT_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, '.corpora', 'repos')

CORPORA = [
    {
        'name': 'mantine',
        'repo': 'mantinedev/mantine',
        'commit': 'e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d',
        'clone': 'mantine',
        'src': 'packages/@mantine/core/src',
        'manager': 'yarn',
    },
    {
        'name': 'chakra',

Props built from React's element attributes keep them in more places: `Pick<DetailedHTMLProps<…>, keyof React.HTMLAttributes<T> | "value">`, a union of props interfaces (bare or inside `Omit`), next/image's global `JSX.IntrinsicElements["img"]` and a generic alias bound to a union of tags (`ComponentPropsWithRef<"h1" | "h2">`) now list the element's attributes as `React.JSX.IntrinsicElements` does, in every `htmlAttributes` mode. For a union of tags, `htmlAttributes: curated` lists each tag's notable attributes together, so a name two tags share is listed once, as the first tag in the union declares it.

138	/// Parse a single file and collect all extractable data.
139	///
140	/// Completely pure — no I/O, no side effects, no cross-file dependencies.
141	/// Safe to call in parallel from rayon workers.
142	///
143	/// Never panics on malformed input: excessive nesting and TypeScript syntax errors
144	/// are reported via `SourceData::diagnostics` rather than failing silently or
145	/// letting the parser overrun the stack.
146	pub fn parse_file(path: &Utf8Path, source: &str) -> SourceData {
147	    let observed_depth = max_bracket_nesting_depth(source);
148	    if observed_depth > MAX_SOURCE_NESTING_DEPTH {
149	        let mut data = SourceData::default();
150	        data.diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
151	            severity: DiagnosticSeverity::Error,
152	            message: format!(
153	                "File exceeds maximum type nesting depth ({observed_depth} > {MAX_SOURCE_NESTING_DEPTH}), skipped to avoid parser stack overflow"
154	            ),
155	            file: Some(path.to_string()),
156	            line: None,
157	            column: None,
158	            help: Some("Reduce nested parenthesized/object/conditional types in this file.".into()),
159	            code: DiagnosticCode::ExcessiveNesting,
160	            affects: Vec::new(),
161	        });
162	        return data;
163	    }
164	
165	    let allocator = Allocator::default();
166	    let source_type = SourceType::from_path(path).unwrap_or_default();
167	    // Parentheses carry no meaning here, and a `ParenthesizedExpression` node would hide the wrapper call beneath it.
168	    let options = ParseOptions { preserve_parens: false, ..ParseOptions::default() };
169	    let ret = Parser::new(&allocator, source, source_type).with_options(options).parse();
170	
171	    // .d.ts declaration files use the same React.FC / ForwardRefExoticComponent patterns as .tsx
172	    let is_tsx = source_type.is_jsx() || source_type.is_typescript_definition();
173	    let mut collector = SourceDataCollector::new(path, source, is_tsx);
174	
175	    // oxc_parser recovers from errors: `ret.program` is usable even with diagnostics, so surface them rather than
176	    // treat the source as clean.
177	    for err in &ret.diagnostics {
178	        collector.data.diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
179	            severity: DiagnosticSeverity::Error,
180	            message: err.to_string(),
181	            file: Some(path.to_string()),
182	            line: None,
183	            column: None,
184	            help: None,
185	            code: DiagnosticCode::ParseError,
186	            affects: Vec::new(),
187	        });
188	    }
189	
190	    // Pass comments by cloning them into owned strings before the allocator drops.
191	    // The comments Vec lives in the arena; we extract them here.
192	    let comments: Vec<OwnedComment> = ret
193	        .program
194	        .comments
195	        .iter()
196	        .map(|c| OwnedComment { span_start: c.span.start, span_end: c.span.end, is_block: c.is_block() })
197	        .collect();
198	    collector.comments = comments;
199	    collector.element_helpers = evidence::element_helpers(&ret.program);
200	    collector.visit_program(&ret.program);
201	    collector.finish()
202	    // allocator drops here — ALL arena memory freed
203	}
